title: Cooke Young Scholars Program
description: Selective five-year, pre-college scholarship for exceptionally promising 7th grade students with financial need. Provides academic and college advising, funding for academic/extracurricular opportunities, Cooke-sponsored summer programs, internships, and a high-achieving peer network through high school and into college preparation. Distinct from the Foundation's separate 'Cooke College Scholarship Program' (a last-dollar award for graduating HS seniors already in ORYN's records) -- this one starts at 7th grade.
application_requirements: grades of mostly A's since 6th grade, no C or below in core subjects
selectivity_evidence: Explicitly 'selective'; 1,348 scholars served to date against presumably many more applicants (exact acceptance rate not published); family adjusted gross income cap around $95,000 per a corroborating source.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read directly by researcher on 2026-08-21. Application is confirmed closed as of this fetch; the next cycle's opening/deadline dates are not posted on this page, left null rather than guessed.

title: The Diana Award
description: Global honour recognizing young people (nominated by others, not self-applied) for sustained social action or humanitarian work aligned with the UN SDGs (Quality Education, Health & Wellbeing, Reduced Inequality, Climate Action). Up to 200 honoured annually across 80+ countries. Not a cash prize -- provides recognition, certification, and networking. Age range (16-24) extends past typical high-school years; relevant mainly to ORYN's older/more-accomplished students with an already-established track record of social action, not a program a younger student can newly join.
application_requirements: nomination by a third party (not self-nominated)
minimum 12 months of sustained social action/humanitarian work
selectivity_evidence: Up to 200 honoured annually out of a global nomination pool across 80+ countries; exact acceptance rate not published.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read directly by researcher on 2026-08-21. This specific page did not state a 2026 nomination deadline; a separate nomination-centre page (not independently re-fetched) referenced 31 Oct 2025 for an earlier cycle -- cycle_status left 'unverified' rather than asserting a current-cycle deadline not confirmed on the page actually read.

title: Prudential Emerging Visionaries
organization: Prudential Financial, in partnership with Ashoka
description: National recognition program (successor to the older 'Prudential Spirit of Community Awards' branding, confirmed via the official Changemakers platform page) for 14-18-year-olds leading innovative projects addressing financial or societal challenges in their communities. Selected Emerging Visionaries may receive up to $15,000 in awards, an all-expenses-paid trip with a parent/guardian to Prudential's Newark HQ, and coaching/skills development.
residency_restrictions: US or Puerto Rico legal residents
application_requirements: project must have started on or before June 1 of the application year
selectivity_evidence: National competitive recognition program, no published acceptance rate.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched (rendered browser, plain WebFetch was 403-blocked) and read directly by researcher on 2026-08-21. The fetched page's visible content is dated to the 2023-2024 cycle ("Through November 2, 2023, the program accepted applications... Meet the 2024 Winners") with no 2026 cycle information shown -- cycle_status deliberately left 'unverified' rather than asserting this is currently open; a future pass should re-check whether the program is still running before treating it as an active 2026/2027 opportunity.
